ARunsLifeOnThePage\nA workflow starts, asks an operator a question and exits while the dashboard is open.\n    The list shows the run each time it speaks: running, blocked on a gate, then ended.
TheListIsOrdered\nThree runs report in the order finished, running, blocked. The list puts the blocked\n    run first, the running one next and the ended one last.

NarrowingTheList
An operator types in the filter box. The list keeps the runs that hold the text in their
    name, repo or node, matches without regard to case or the spaces around it, and shows every
    run again once the box is cleared.

TheAttendantIsSwitchedOnThePage\nAn operator opens Settings, ticks the attendant box, clears it, and goes back to the\n    runs. The pane names the mode each time, and the mode is kept across the return.

ReadingABlockedRun
A run asks the operator a question. The operator opens the run, sees the gate it waits on, and
    types an answer. groom cannot reach the run's workspace, so it refuses the answer and says why,
    and the run stays blocked on the list.

LookingThroughThePanes
An operator walks the left bar. History lists no ended run, the attendant has sent an agent at
    nothing, no dispatch queue is configured, and the settings pane opens. The run list is where
    they come back to.

- **(none)**: the list holds no run of ours. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **running**: the run reported progress and holds no gate. Reached by: ReportProgress r00.
- **blocked**: the run waits on one gate. Reached by: ReportGate r01.
- **finished**: the run exited with a code. Reached by: ReportExit r02.
- **Off**: no attendant answers the gates. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **Headless**: an attendant answers the gates. Reached by: SwitchTheAttendant attendant on.

kept in the home config of the groom the book runs against.

A run reaches groom by a workflow pushing it, not by anything the dashboard does, so the page book arranges a run by
the same three pushes the HTTP book uses and then reads the list. The check suggests asking the HTTP book for the run
with Needs. The page book keeps its own pushes because the push is the event the page is judged against: it must
show the run the moment groom takes the push, over its own socket, and a Needs would arrange the run before the page
opened.

sources: groom/groom/assets/dashboard.js, groom/groom/app.py::_handle_command, groom/groom/gates.py::answer_gate
The detail pane of a blocked run holds the gate it waits on and a box for the answer. The answer travels over the
dashboard socket, and groom writes it into the gate file of the run's workspace. A pushed run has no workspace, so
groom refuses and the page shows a notice, "answer not taken", with the reason groom gave. The page's refusal is the
same sentence the HTTP book's AnswerGate gives for the same run, so the page book states it as one rule and the notice
carries its last line.

The page is one document with five panes, chosen by the button of the left bar that is pressed: runs, history, the
attendant, dispatch and settings. Each pane reads its own HTTP route when it opens. The book's groom holds no ended
run, no attendance and no dispatch queue, so History, Attendant and Dispatch each show their empty line, and the
pane's button of the left bar is the interaction that reaches it. The page opens on the run list.

elements: FilterTheList
sources: groom/groom/assets/dashboard.js, groom/groom/projection.py::matches
The run list is filtered in the browser, on the fleet the socket already pushed, and not by asking groom: a list
filtered by the server would be replaced by the next push. The page trims what is typed, ignores its case, and keeps a
run when the text is part of its name, repo, node, the gate path it waits on or its id. The HTTP read of the fleet
filters too, in projection.matches, and the two books state their own filter.
